Georgina Energy plc
("Georgina", "Georgina Energy" or the "Company")
Hussar EP513 Seismic Implementation
Georgina Energy Plc, (LSE: GEX.L), a helium, hydrogen and natural gas exploration and development company with strategic permits in Australia, advises that due to delays in mobilising the Ensign Rig 970 to site, The company has decided to implement a new seismic program, subject to regulatory approvals to conduct additional non-invasive seismic over the Hussar Prospect which will be fully funded by Harlequin Energy Limited. (https://www.harlequin-energy.com/)
A review of the geophysical attributes of vintage seismic over the Hussar Prospect by Distinguished Emeritus Professor, Dr Brian Evans, of Curtin University, has revealed the interpreted presence of “Direct Helium and Hydrogen Indicators” (“DHHIs”) where they are manifested as “bright spots, phase reversals or gas chimneys.” (https://geoexpro.com/acquiring-seismic-data-for-oil-exploration-in-1980-but-using-it-to-find-hydrogen-now/)
As a result of the delays in mobilising the Ensign Rig 970 to site caused by adverse weather conditions and road closures to heavy vehicles the Company has designed a c.350 km seismic survey over the Hussar Prospect to further and more accurately delineate the DHHIs interpreted by Professor Evans and to provide even more clarity over the all important salt sealing layer overlying the main Townsend and fractured basement target zones.
The seismic is planned to not require heavy vehicle access by utilising the very latest state of the art light weight seismic techniques and equipment that are environmentally non-invasive.
Such equipment will not require any clearing or grading of seismic lines nor extended geophone cables but will use carefully modulated vibration sources able to be mounted on light weight rubber tyred or crawler tractors. This equipment will also utilise newer generation nodal ecosystems utilising integrated
Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
or wireless transceivers for contactless, daily data harvesting.
The seismic programme will take approximately 30 days field work and will take place subject to Western Australian Department of Mines, Petroleum and Exploration and Traditional Owner cultural heritage approvals expected to be issued shortly.
This programme is also designed with a view to efficiently expedite rapid field development with multiple wells into production and export subject to commercial discovery success.
Planned c.350 line km of new seismic Hussar Prospect
Lightweight non-invasive seismic vibration source
Cable free Bluetooth seismic node (geophone)
The Hussar EP513 prospect re-entry in Exploration Permit 513 in the Officer Basin in Western Australia is primarily targeting subsalt reservoir formations, including the Townsend Formation and fractured Neoproterozoic basement lithologies, for helium, hydrogen and natural gas and is planned to drill to a Total Depth of approximately 3,200m which may be extended depending on gas occurrences and reservoir quality. Globally, fractured basement reservoirs similar to that targeted in the Hussar Prospect, have proven to be prolific producers. The Bach Ho field in fractured basement offshore Vietnam for example, at its peak produced 1.6 BCFGE (billion cubic feet of gas equivalent) per day and has been in continuous production for over 40 years. (
https://www.saltworkconsultants.com/downloads/Bach_Ho_Cuong_Warren_09.pdf
)
A secondary target is the hydrocarbon gas potential in the Kanpa and Hussar formations overlying the primary subsalt targets. These formations have not been adequately tested to date but have shown excellent porosities and hydrocarbon shows during previous drilling.
The Hussar prospect has an Independent Geological Report dated 1
st
February 2026 by Competent Person Mr Maki Petkovski certifying unrisked SPE PRMS (the Society of Petroleum Engineers and Petroleum Resource Management Systems) net attributable 2U Prospective Resources of 283 BCF helium, 315 BCF hydrogen and 2.93 TCF of hydrocarbon gas.
Based on the pricing of Helium US$450/MCFG and Hydrogen US$2.65/kg and US$8/MCF for hydrocarbon gas, these volumes would equate to a total potential combined net attributable unrisked potential in-situ value of c.
US$152
billion.
These are estimates
in-situ values from the AER (Australian Energy Regulator) and HNT (Helium Price Index) developed by the Company
based on unrisked prospective resources; they exclude production, separation and transport-to-market costs, and there is no certainty that any part of these resources will be commercially recovered.
Further updates will follow as we progress towards a revised spud date along with additional site photos which can be viewed by shareholders on the Georgina website.
Anthony Hamilton, Chief Executive Officer of Georgina Energy, commented:
“This seismic programme was originally planned as a post drill program but due to weather and road closures will provide multiple benefits in not only amplifying Direct Helium and Hydrogen seismic indicators but also in potential full field development. Of this exciting prospect and we look forward to making further announcements in due course”.

Georgina Energy plc
("Georgina", "Georgina Energy" or the "Company")
Hussar EP513 Prospect Update
Georgina Energy Plc, (LSE: GEX.L), a helium, hydrogen and natural gas exploration and development company with strategic permits in Australia, confirms that civil engineering contractors have completed all pre-drill site and road access works to enable the contracted Ensign 970 drill rig to test of this exciting prospect, which has 330 km² of areal closure and is one of the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbons prospects remaining untested in onshore Australia.
Highlights
The drilling pad, water well, Turkey’s nest and sump are completed and lined with waterproof sheeting.
The water well has been completed and tested on a long term test delivering some 260,000 litres per day.
The 20 inch conductor pipe has been drilled and cemented in place.
The Hussar airstrip has been cleared, gravelled and rolled to provide a 1,400m length airstrip capable of operation in virtually any weather.
Access roads have been cleared, graded and gravelled and compacted where necessary.
Mobilisation planning with the Ensign Rig 970 has been almost completed.
Delays for Drill program
The civil engineers and water well drillers have begun demobilising from site however there has been unseasonal record-breaking rain in the district which has prevented all of the contractors’ equipment and trucks being able to demobilise. The Company remained optimistic along with Ensign that mobilisation would occur in September as planned but the continuing road closures have further complicated the program along with flooding.
Leonora, a town close to the start of the main access road recorded a record-breaking 58.8mm of rain in the 24 hours to 9:00 am on Monday, September 7, 2026. This resulted in:
The wettest September day on record for a month that typically averages less than 10mm.
The heaviest spring daily rainfall ever recorded in Leonora.
The wettest day overall in nine years, delivering over a quarter of the town's average annual rainfall in just one day.
The second-wettest September on record for the town overall in 129 years of data collection.
Ongoing road closures in within the Wiluna Shire Council:
www.wiluna.wa.gov.au
Ongoing restrictions on heavy vehicle access (RAV-Restricted Access Vehicles):
www.wiluna.wa.gov.au
have prevented any movement of overwidth, over length or over weight vehicles at any times when roads are wet. This means that prime movers hauling triple trailers are banned from large sections of the road network to Hussar within the Shire.
The Company have held ongoing discussions with Ensign Drilling and both parties have concluded that the mobilisation of the drilling rig to the Hussar site represents an extraordinarily high chance of being halted “en route” currently. Furthermore, the Company risks incurring material standby charges from not only Ensign but the other service contractors necessarily involved in this operation which would make any continuing delays costly especially as such time delays cannot be reliably forecast in the current circumstances.
The Company is hopeful of mobilising the drilling rig and associated service contractors in a timely fashion subject to safety constraints including the weather and road conditions to allow for the safe mobilisation of the equipment and personnel.
Further updates will follow as we progress towards a revised spud date with additional site photos which can be viewed by shareholders on the Georgina website.
Anthony Hamilton, Chief Executive Officer of Georgina Energy, commented:
“Georgina’s contractors have done an excellent job of preparing the site and access roads to enable the mobilisation of the Ensign 970 drill rig to enable the drill testing of this exciting prospect, however, unexpected heavy rainfall and road closures have caused the targeted drill program to be delayed and we look forward to making further announcements in due course.”

These works, including already completed site and camp pad preparation, represent another key step forward in advancing the planned drilling programme at the Hussar prospect.
Highlights
The twenty inch conductor pipe has been set and will be cemented in the 26-inch hole opening.
The water well drill rig has completed the water well drilling with a consistent flow rate.
Gravelling, rolling and compacting of the drilling and camp pads has been completed.
The Hussar airstrip has been extended for Medevac and crew changes and has been completely rolled, compacted and a low spot prone to waterlogging has been gravelled and compacted.
Gravel has been carted to the main access road and laying and compacting of several low spots prone to flooding has commenced.
All the pre-drilling site works are expected to be completed shortly.
With 330 km² of areal closure at 3U level, the Hussar prospect ranks among the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbon prospects onshore Australia that remains untested. The Hussar prospect has an Independent Geological Report dated 1
st

US$152 billion.
Note:
These are estimated “in-situ” values from the AER (Australian Energy Regulator) and HNT (Helium Price Index) developed by the Company based on unrisked 2U SPE PRMS (Society of Petroleum Engineers Petroleum Resources Management) Prospective (recoverable) Resources; they exclude production, separation and transport-to-market costs, and there is no certainty that all or any part of these Prospective Recoverable Resources will be commercially recovered.

Globally, fractured basement reservoirs similar to that targeted in the Hussar Prospect, have proven to be prolific producers. The Bach Ho field in fractured basement offshore Vietnam for example, at its peak produced 1.6 BCFGE (billion cubic feet of gas equivalent) per day and has been in continuous production for over 40 years. (
https://www.saltworkconsultants.com/downloads/Bach_Ho_Cuong_Warren_09.pdf

A secondary target is the hydrocarbon gas potential in the Kanpa and Hussar formations overlying the primary subsalt targets. These formations have not been adequately tested to date but have shown excellent porosities and hydrocarbon shows during previous drilling.

Completion of £1.25 Million Fundraise
Georgina Energy plc (LSE: GEX), is pleased to announce that it has successfully raised £1.25m through the issue of 10,000,000 new ordinary shares at a placing price of 12.5 pence per share (the "Placing"). The Company will issue investors with one warrant per one placing share at an exercise price of 14 pence expiring 5 years from Admission ("Investor Warrants").
Use of Proceeds
The net proceeds of the Placing will be used to advance Mount Winter and for general working capital.
Broker Warrants
The Company will issue 600,000 Broker Warrants exercisable at 12 pence and expire five years from the date of Admission.
Admission of Placing Shares
An application has been made for
10,000,000
new ordinary shares to be admitted to trading on the official list and main market of the London Stock Exchange from 8.00 a.m. on 2 September 2026 ("Admission").
Total Voting Rights
In accordance with the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules, the Company confirms that following Admission, the Company's enlarged issued ordinary share capital will comprise 280,861,707 Ordinary Shares. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in Treasury. Therefore, following Admission, the above figure may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations to determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in the Company, under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

company_30s.what_they_do: Hussar Energy is a junior exploration firm focused on developing the EP513 prospect in the UK. They drill wells, run seismic surveys, and look for hydrocarbons in the North Sea basin.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The North Sea remains a key source of oil and gas for Europe, and new discoveries help secure supply and support the transition to low‑carbon fuels. Hussar’s EP513 target sits in a region that has seen several successful finds, giving the company a realistic chance to add value to the sector.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the exploration phase, having just completed a £1.25 million raise and a new water‑well installation. It is cash‑burning but has secured enough capital to keep drilling and seismic work underway. The stock is trading at a very low price, far below what most analysts would consider a healthy valuation for an asset‑rich explorer.

rns_narrative: Hussar has been rolling out a steady stream of operational updates: a new seismic program, a water‑well completion, and a small‑scale drill mobilisation. The latest RNS confirms the company is moving from planning to execution, signalling a shift from fundraising to field activity.

The narrative clusters around three themes: 1) Capital deployment – the company is putting the newly raised money into real work; 2) Technical progress – seismic and drilling milestones are being hit; 3) Governance – the AGM and share‑award exercises show the board is keeping shareholders in the loop.
These events suggest the firm is stabilising after a period of uncertainty. The focus is now on generating data that could lead to a commercial licence or a first‑production announcement.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: quiet optimism – the community is largely silent but a handful of insiders see potential upside.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few traders (e.g., deltalo) are touting the company’s partnership with Harlequin Energy and the new seismic work as a sign that a breakthrough could be imminent.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some voices doubt the company’s existence and warn of delays, citing the absence of a clear production plan and the risk that the EP513 prospect may not pay off.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The sentiment has stayed flat; no new surge of hype or panic. The silence is the biggest signal – no one is talking, so a catalyst could create a surprise move.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no public interest. That means a catalyst could trigger a big surprise move.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the first well at EP513 – if the well returns a decent cut‑off depth, it could unlock a licence.
Positive seismic interpretation – a clear hydrocarbon indicator would attract larger partners or a buy‑out.
A follow‑on funding round or a partnership with a bigger producer to share the risk and bring in expertise.
A regulatory approval or a change in local oil‑and‑gas policy that reduces costs or expands the permissible area for drilling.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden volume spike on the stock, a sharp rise in the share price after an RNS, or a shift in the few social posts from neutral to bullish. A clear positive comment from an industry analyst would also be a good trigger.
expect_next.timing_regime: The price is still deep in the bottom of a crash. If the recent operational news is the first real sign of progress, the stock is likely in the early capitulation phase. A mean‑reversion bounce would need a catalyst that proves the asset is viable – the seismic results or first well data are the most likely triggers.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is in a deep crash; if the EP513 well or seismic data proves promising, the market will react strongly. A recovery to the 52‑week midpoint could generate a 50‑70% upside, matching the historical return profile of similar deep‑bottom signals. The asymmetry is clear: the downside is capped at the current price, while the upside comes from a return to mid‑range levels.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the EP513 target is a non‑producer or that drilling costs outpace the capital raised. A failed well or a regulatory setback could push the share price back to the bottom, leaving investors with a near‑total loss.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: up to 100% of the invested capital (the stock could fall to zero). Potential gain: 50‑70% if the price climbs to the 52‑week midpoint, giving an asymmetry of roughly 1:2.5 in favour of upside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the recent low, sizing 10–15% of your capital per trade. Place a stop 5% below the low to protect against a further crash. Use a trailing stop that locks in gains once the price reaches the 52‑week midpoint.
